speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a concerning rash and recent health changes; let's start by asking: when did the rash first appear, and has it spread to any other parts of your body?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with a rash that started last night, finding it very concerning. He does not recall being exposed to any new environmental stimuli such as detergents or plants like poison ivy. He mentions he recently started seeing a primary care provider for arthritis management and a new onset cough.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. You mentioned a new onset cough and a recent start of arthritis management; are you currently taking any new medications, specifically sulfonamides or anticonvulsants? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Liver_Function_Tests.

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood and liver tests are normal. Besides the cough and arthritis, have you noticed any joint pain, fever, or fatigue lately? Did the rash appear on your face, hands, or trunk?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on the upper half of the back. I also have Concern over sudden onset, Recent cough, Unaware of exposure to new environmental stimuli, Mucositis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS). The combination of a rash on the upper back, mucositis, and recent initiation of arthritis medication (likely a sulfonamide) with a new cough is highly suggestive of an acute hypersensitivity reaction. Given the severity, please proceed to hospital admission for supportive care.
